::: {.callout-note}
## Packages containing datasets that cannot be shared

This criterion is recommended in general. For packages that do not contain all datasets needed because some cannot be shared, it becomes a core criterion: without a third-party certification, only the Tier 1 criteria are assessed, so the package can get at most Bronze. With a certification, the core criteria that need the data are rated from the certificate, so Silver and Gold become possible. See rules 3 and 4 in [Rules of the badge system](../../pipeline.qmd#rules-of-the-badge-system).
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Who counts as independent

An independent party is someone who is not an author of the paper and had no part in its data collection or analysis. The certificate or signed letter must state the reproducer's name, affiliation and relationship to the authors, what was reproduced, and how.
:::

## Rating

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Met"}
The package includes a certification that an independent, disinterested party reproduced all results (or specified tables and figures) from the package, e.g. a signed letter by the reproducer or a certificate from a certification agency, stating what was reproduced and how.
:::
::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple" title="Partially met"}
A certification is provided, but it covers only some of the results, does not state what was reproduced, or comes from a party that is not independent of the authors.
:::
::: {.callout-important appearance="simple" title="Not met"}
No third-party certification is provided when the data are confidential and the reproducer cannot access them.
:::

[Based on: [#131](../../sources.qmd#p131 "Guide for Accelerating Computational Reproducibility in the Social Sciences") only (ACRE, adjusting levels for confidential/proprietary data); see also [#52](../../sources.qmd#p52 "CODECHECK: an open science initiative for the independent execution of computations underlying research articles during peer review to improve reproducibility") CODECHECK certificate, [#56](../../sources.qmd#p56 "Reproducibility badging and definitions") ROR-R badge.]{.source-note}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Not applicable"}
All datasets needed for reproduction are included the package (C2)
:::

**[#131](../../sources.qmd#p131)** Guide for Accelerating Computational Reproducibility in the Social Sciences · *injunctive*

> "...the authors provide a certification that a third party was able to reproduce the display item (or the paper as a whole) from the analysis data (CRA). Such certification may include a signed letter by a disinterested reproducer or a certificate from a certification agency for data and code" (https://bitss.github.io/ACRE/assessment.html\#adjusting-levels-to-account-for-confidentialproprietary-data)

*Note:* especially for proprietary data
